name: Diagnosis Question Tree – Marine
description: One decision tree per species that leads to the most likely disease with at most 13 yes/no questions. Based on the diseases and signs from diseases-saltwater.json.
rules: Only questions about appearance, behaviour, history and water parameters – no questions that require opening or a necropsy of the animal.
Every path ends after at most 13 questions.
The result is a probability estimate, not a diagnosis. Several diseases can occur at the same time.
disclaimer: Not a substitute for a veterinary examination. Many pathogens can only be reliably distinguished by a smear under the microscope.

usage.tree: Start at species[id].treeId: ask the 'question' of a node, go to 'yes' for yes and 'no' for no. A node with 'result' is the outcome.
usage.unknownAnswer: For 'don't know' switch to the matrix evaluation: start with the species' priorWeights (plus '_none' with weight 3), normalised. Each answered question multiplies each disease's value by P(yes) or 1−P(yes) from the matrix, then renormalise. Next question = unanswered question with the largest information gain (entropy). Stop at probability ≥ 0.8, when no question yields at least 0.05 bits, or after 13 questions.
usage.defaultProbabilities: If a question is missing from a disease's matrix: 0.03 (specific sign), 0.2 (non-specific sign), 0.4 (eats normally).
usage.speciesSigns: After the result, show the species-specific recognition signs from species[id].speciesSigns[diseaseId].
usage.rareCombination: Leaves with rareCombination=true were shortened because of a very unlikely combination of answers – continue with the matrix evaluation here.
usage.measurable: Questions with 'measurable' can be answered from measured values. Parameters and units are listed in 'parameters'. Condition: compare the parameter value using 'op' (<, <=, >, >=, ==, !=) against 'value' or against the species value in 'ref' (e.g. species.temp.idealMin from the species list). 'logic' any = one condition is enough, all = all must apply. 'expression' is the same rule in short form. mode auto: if no condition applies, the answer is no. mode partial: if a condition applies, the answer is yes; otherwise ask the manual part ('manualQuestion'). Conditions whose species value is empty (null) are skipped. Missing measurements: with logic any, one available condition that applies is enough for yes; a no (mode auto) requires all values. If it cannot be decided this way, ask the question as usual.

validation: Simulation with 300 random, matrix-conforming cases per disease and tree; checks internal consistency only, not real-world accuracy.

nh4.label: Ammonium/ammonia (total as measured by test kit)

carbon_in_filter.label: Activated carbon running permanently in the filter

after_med.text: Did the problems occur shortly after adding medication, fertiliser or copper?

measurable.manualQuestion: Was medication or fertiliser added recently?
measurable.note: Limit according to UF/IFAS FA165: return invertebrates only at no more than 0.01 mg/L copper. Medication and fertiliser cannot be measured.

anemone_white.text: Is the anemone bleached white or translucent?

black_dots.text: Are there small black spots on the body or fins?

carbon.text: Is activated carbon (especially lignite-based) running permanently in the filter?

measurable.note: Taken from the tank equipment. The type of carbon (lignite) is not distinguished.

cauliflower.text: Are there granular, cauliflower-like white to pink nodules on the fins or skin?

cloudy_skin.text: Does the skin look milky-grey or bluish clouded (lots of mucus)?

dust.text: Is there a very fine gold, rust or powder-coloured coating like dust on the body?
dust.hint: Shine a torch at an angle from the side – the coating is much finer than individual spots.

eats_normally.text: Does the animal eat normally and otherwise behave inconspicuously?

fin_rot.text: Are fin edges frayed or milky, or are the fins getting shorter?

flashing.text: Does the fish rub itself against rocks, substrate or plants?

gills.text: Is the fish breathing conspicuously fast, or are the gill covers flared?

head_pits.text: Are there small holes, pits or pale skin lesions on the head or along the lateral line?

mucus_shreds.text: Is a thick mucus layer forming that peels off the skin in shreds?

new_animals.text: Were new animals or plants added without quarantine in the last 4 weeks?

params_out_of_range.text: Are temperature, pH, general hardness (GH) or carbonate hardness (KH) outside the species' range?
params_out_of_range.hint: Compare with the species' minimum and maximum values.

measurable.expression: temp < species.temp.min || temp > species.temp.max || ph < species.ph.min || ph > species.ph.max || gh < species.gh.min || gh > species.gh.max || kh < species.kh.min || kh > species.kh.max
measurable.note: Compared with the species' min/max values from the species list. Conditions whose species value is empty (e.g. GH in marine species = null) are skipped.

red_lesions.text: Are there red haemorrhages, reddened areas or open ulcers?

sudden_deaths.text: Have several animals died within a few days?

wasting.text: Has the animal been losing weight for weeks even though it eats?

water_bad.text: Is ammonium/ammonia or nitrite detectable, or is nitrate clearly elevated?

measurable.note: '> 0' means: detectable with the test kit. The nitrate limit of 50 mg/L is a guide value and can be adjusted in the app.

white_spots.text: Are there white spots like grains of salt or sugar (up to approx. 1 mm) on the skin or fins?
white_spots.hint: Look closely at pale or dark scaleless fish; check the fin edges.
